solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: During prohibition, show disapproval of primate

indicators.note: one thing happening during another sits within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition
to boo is to jeer in disapproval

explanation.surface: A primate gets jeered at while some prohibition is in force.
explanation.definitionFit: The baboon is a large African monkey, one kind of primate.

clue.text: Subtle changes in old garment

indicators.note: changes tells us the letters of the word before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Small alterations made to a period item of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges the six letters of SUBTLE. A bustle was a frame worn under the back of a Victorian skirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A bustle is a padded frame once worn beneath a skirt, an article of dress from the past.

clue.text: Girl, one after boy from southern Asia

indicators.note: after places the girl and the one behind the boy in the answer

parts.note: Ben is a boy's name
gal is an informal word for a girl
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A girl and someone else follow a boy who comes from south Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue names the girl first, but 'after' sends her and the one behind the boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Bengali describes someone or something from Bengal, a region of Bangladesh and eastern India in South Asia.

clue.text: Written in memo, a thoughtless promise

indicators.note: written in means the letters are sitting within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A rash pledge set down in an office note.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'memO, A THoughtless'.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath is a solemn vow or pledge.

clue.text: Successful striker, one making one's mark?

definitions.meaning: a footballer who puts the ball in the net
someone who scores, that is cuts or scratches a mark on something

explanation.surface: A goal-getting forward who leaves an impression.
explanation.definitionFit: A goalscorer is a striker who succeeds, and to score is also to scratch a line, so a scorer leaves marks.

clue.text: Little time invested in needlework, note

indicators.note: invested in means one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: crochet is needlework done with a hooked needle
t is the short form of time

explanation.surface: Not much time is put into a piece of needlework, the clue observes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' is the definition, a musical one, not a written message.
explanation.definitionFit: A crotchet is a musical note worth one beat, called a quarter note in American usage.

clue.text: Arm in error, if leg!

indicators.note: in means the letters are found within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A cricket umpire's mistake over a leg-before appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'erroR IF LEg'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle is a firearm, and arm is a standard word for a weapon.

clue.text: Something unusual I try to change under artist

indicators.note: in a down answer, under puts the second piece below the first

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: to change tells us the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tries a novel trick while studying under a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges I TRY into RITY, which goes under RA.
explanation.definitionFit: A rarity is a thing seldom found or seen.

clue.text: Problem brewing artisan beer

indicators.note: brewing means the letters are being stirred into a new mixture

explanation.surface: A small craft brewer making beer runs into difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewing' rearranges the eleven letters of ARTISAN BEER.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainteaser is a puzzle, a problem set to test the mind.

clue.text: Funny reason to embrace democrat in the end, US politician

indicators.note: to embrace means one piece holds the other inside it
funny suggests the letters behave oddly, so they are rearranged
in the end picks out the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Washington lawmaker finds an odd reason to back a Democrat at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' rearranges REASON into SENAOR; 'in the end' takes T from democrat, which 'to embrace' puts inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator sits in the US Senate, the upper chamber of Congress.

clue.text: Sovereign added to rotten bid

indicators.note: added to puts the sovereign onto the end of the rotten piece

parts.note: food that is off has gone bad
ER is the royal cipher, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A monarch's name is attached to a poor attempt.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is crossword shorthand for the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A bid and an offer are both a price put forward.

clue.text: Star element

definitions.meaning: the ... role, or the person who plays it
the heavy metal with symbol Pb

explanation.definitionFit: The lead in a film is its principal performer, and lead is a chemical element, a soft grey metal.

clue.text: Cautious individual, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear means a word is said aloud and we write down what it sounds like

parts.note: discrete means separate or individual

explanation.surface: A careful person, someone reports.
explanation.walkthrough: Two words with the same sound: the one meaning separate stands for the one meaning tactful.
explanation.definitionFit: Discreet means careful not to give offence or reveal secrets, so it is cautious in what one says.

clue.text: Massive caper briefly following concert

indicators.note: following puts the caper piece after the concert in the answer

parts.note: a gig is a live music performance

indicators.note: briefly means the last letter is cut off the word

parts.note: antics are capers, playful tricks

explanation.surface: A huge prank pulled after a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: Gigantic means enormous, as massive as a giant.

clue.text: Tart up for this fantasy?

parts.note: a pie is a baked pastry like a tart
up in the sky, aloft

explanation.surface: A pastry tossed upward as part of a daydream.
explanation.walkthrough: A pie up in the air is literally where the phrase puts it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pie in the sky is an idiom for an unrealistic hope or empty promise.

clue.text: Desire in boy to see galley

indicators.note: in means the first piece goes inside the second

parts.note: Ken is a boy's name
an itch is a restless longing

explanation.surface: A young lad longs to visit a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A galley is the cooking area on a ship or aircraft.

clue.text: Wrong keeping shed enclosed

indicators.note: keeping means one piece holds the other within it

parts.note: a sin is a wrong
a hut is a simple shed

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer stays sealed inside a garden shed.
explanation.definitionFit: Shut in means confined or kept within walls.

clue.text: Quite alluring

explanation.definitionFit: Pretty works as an adverb for rather or fairly, and as an adjective for attractive.

clue.text: Carving of mahogany for Scottish festival

indicators.note: carving reshapes a piece of wood, so the letters of the word are reshaped

explanation.surface: A wooden carving made for a celebration north of the border.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogmanay is the Scottish celebration of New Year's Eve.

clue.text: Noise coming from good little piggy?

parts.note: the runt is the smallest pig in a litter

explanation.surface: A sound made by a well-behaved piglet.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's pig is apt, as a grunt is the sound a pig makes.
explanation.definitionFit: A grunt is a low guttural sound, the kind a pig makes.

clue.text: Mix porridge

definitions.meaning: British slang for time served in prison

explanation.definitionFit: To stir is to blend, and stir is slang for prison, as is porridge, the title of a British prison sitcom.

clue.text: Some crockery I'd upset: don't say a word!

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the word is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: sh is a call for silence

explanation.surface: Someone who has knocked over the plates begs for secrecy.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish is a bowl or plate, an item of crockery.

clue.text: Hope last seen of apparent decay

indicators.note: last seen of picks out the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: rust is the corrosion of metal

explanation.surface: The final glimpse of visible decay, with some hope remaining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last seen of' takes T from apparent.
explanation.definitionFit: To trust is to hope or believe confidently, as in trusting all is well.

clue.text: Ultimately, prerogative mine to assume the nickname

indicators.note: ultimately picks out the final letter of the word
to assume means to take on, so one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: Taking on a nickname is, in the end, a person's own right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' is not a link word here: it is fodder, taken inside the mine.
explanation.definitionFit: An epithet is a descriptive name added to a person's name, a byname.

clue.text: See anything but frozen water

parts.note: not, as in not at all
ice is water that has frozen

explanation.surface: Look at anything except ice.
explanation.definitionFit: To notice is to observe or spot something.

clue.text: Drink reserved, also bottled

indicators.note: bottled means the second piece is held inside the first

parts.note: shy means reserved or timid
and adds something, meaning also

explanation.surface: A drink kept aside and put in a bottle too.
explanation.definitionFit: Shandy is a British drink of beer mixed with lemonade.
